children.description: Row=implicit multiplication/juxtaposition (no separator between children). AlignedRows.children is the legacy pre-2D fallback only. List=a bare ","-separated list of complete expressions.

rows.description: Canonical two-dimensional AlignedRows layout. Each item is an AlignedRow.

cells.description: Cells in one AlignedRow, split by LaTeX alignment tabs (&).

delimiter.description: Only present on Parenthesized. "("=real parentheses, "|"=absolute value, "{"=escaped literal curly braces (e.g. set notation \{2,4,6\}, or a \cases block opened as \left\{...\right.), "["=square brackets (e.g. an interval). Not the \sqrt[n]{...} index bracket, which is Radical's separate `index` field.

environment.description: Only present on AlignedRows, and only when the row split came from inside a \begin{name}...\end{name} block (e.g. "cases", "aligned", "array", "matrix"); omitted for a bare 'a \\ b' row split outside any environment. Downstream presentation (braille/TTS) needs this because there is no single universal rule for 'multiple rows' -- piecewise/cases, aligned equation chains, and matrices are each presented differently.

notation.description: Only present on Fraction, and only for a bare "a/b" slash-notation fraction (not the default \frac{}{} stacked form, which omits this field entirely). Presentation layers need this because the braille regulation gives slash-notation fractions a different indicator cell from the stacked form's bar.
